title: South Korea Strengthens Industrial Spy Laws to Protect Chip Secrets from China
detail: South Korea is ramping up its industrial espionage laws to protect semiconductor trade secrets amid growing concerns over chip technology theft by China. The legislative push targets the protection of South Korea's critical semiconductor intellectual property as geopolitical competition over advanced chip technology intensifies. The move reflects Seoul's effort to safeguard its dominant position in memory chips and advanced semiconductor manufacturing from foreign intelligence-gathering operations.

title: Lee's Approval Rating Falls Below 40% for First Time, Gallup Korea Finds
detail: A Gallup Korea poll of 1,000 respondents released September 11 put President Lee Jae-myung's job approval at 38%, the first time it has fallen below 40% since his June 2025 inauguration. Disapproval held at 51%. The slide is driven by disputes over Cabinet nominees — 43% called Justice Minister nominee Kim Seung-won unfit amid stock-manipulation and abuse-of-power allegations, and 61% viewed Gender Equality Minister nominee Yong Hye-in as unsuitable after she said she would keep her parliamentary seat if appointed — compounded by the housing affordability crisis and economic hardship. The same poll found 55% opposed to deploying South Korean troops to the Strait of Hormuz.
